papers.title_in_file: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks for Multi-Channel Supervised Learning
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study proposing quantum convolutional kernels that handle multi-channel image data and comparing them with a control QCNN and prior quantum models on CIFAR-10 and synthetic data.

assertions.value: The authors report that binary CIFAR classification reached 94.5% with the best proposed model against 85.0% for a control QCNN, and that with all ten classes the CO-QCNN reached 34.9% against 28.2% for the control.
quotes: accuracy of 94.5%, compared to 85.0% with the control QCNN. When trained on all ten
classes, the CO-QCNN was able to achieve 34.9% while the control QCNN produced
28.2% accuracy using U1.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulated study on a reduced training set.
assertions.reader_inference: Section 4.2 shows a reduced, downsized dataset (first 500 training points per class, images reduced in size), so the percentages are not comparable to full benchmarks.

assertions.value: The authors state that CO-QCNN, PCO-QCNN and WEV-QCNN achieve state-of-the-art accuracy compared to current quantum neural networks, and that CNN-P is a classical CNN with the same number of parameters as their work.
